verdict.headline: A genuinely quiet run.
verdict.detail: A genuinely quiet run. Not one transfer has settled and not one listing has appeared since the 18:44Z briefing, so the position, the market and every open call stand exactly as they were. The one new fact is a reversal rather than an action: Manuel Neuer's block is lifted — all four of its reversal conditions are now met on dated evidence — and he is still not a buy, for reasons that have nothing to do with the block. Nothing requires Georg tonight. The live Hansen bid runs to early tomorrow afternoon, the three flips settle the day after the lock, and the lineup should be left exactly as it is set.

sell.reason: No sale is recommended before the lock, and none is needed — the balance is comfortably positive and nothing has to be funded tonight. The standing Wolf sale remains correct on merit and remains deferred: the probable XI again leaves him out of his club's eleven for a third consecutive run, so his block reversal is still unmet, but he is the fourth midfielder that keeps the alternative shape legal and selling him before the lock would cost more than it raises. Execute it after the lock. One housekeeping item is outstanding from an earlier run and has not been done: the Hwang ask is still sitting on the market at a wide premium on a falling asset. The instruction was to pull it, not to sell him. It is unlikely to clear at that price, but if it did before the lock it would strip an attacker out of a squad that has no spare one, so pull it when convenient.

buy.reason: Hansen is the only points buy and it is already placed and live — the merit was hardened two runs ago, the probable XI again puts his surname in his club's back line, and he settles comfortably before the lock so he is fieldable for MD9. Nothing on the board beats him and nothing new has been listed since the last run. Neuer is the one item worth reading in full. His block is reversed outright: the ask is exactly at market value, two dated sources from the fourth and fifth of November put him back from the foot-tendon problem and name him as his club's starting keeper for this matchday, his average beats the keeper he would displace by a clear margin, and the balance has room. No future run may cite that block as a fitness or selection objection again. He is nevertheless an avoid, on three grounds outside it: his listing settles after the lock so the upgrade buys nothing this matchday; his market value is in the falling band, so every day of waiting makes him cheaper and the first matchday he could actually be fielded is a fortnight away; and capturing the upgrade at all would mean selling a confirmed starting keeper who returned a big score on his one recent appearance. Buying him tonight would be paying today's price for a player who cannot be used until he is cheaper.
